claims.text: Stomach regions: cardia, fundus, body and pylorus.
claims.quote: There are four main regions in the stomach: the cardia, fundus, body, and pylorus

claims.text: Cardia and fundus: the cardia is where the esophagus joins; the dome-shaped fundus sits under the diaphragm, above and left of the cardia.
claims.quote: The cardia (or cardiac region) is the point where the esophagus connects to the stomach and through which food passes into the stomach. Located inferior to the diaphragm, above and to the left of the cardia, is the dome-shaped fundus.

claims.text: Pylorus: funnel-shaped; connects the stomach to the duodenum.
claims.quote: The funnel-shaped pylorus connects the stomach to the duodenum.

claims.text: Small intestine: duodenum, jejunum, ileum (proximal to distal).
claims.quote: From proximal (at the stomach) to distal, these are the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum

claims.text: Duodenum: the shortest part (25.4 cm); it starts at the pyloric sphincter, passes behind the peritoneum (retroperitoneal) and curves in a C around the head of the pancreas.
claims.quote: The shortest region is the 25.4-cm (10-in) duodenum, which begins at the pyloric sphincter. Just past the pyloric sphincter, it bends posteriorly behind the peritoneum, becoming retroperitoneal, and then makes a C-shaped curve around the head of the pancreas before ascending anteriorly again to return to the peritoneal cavity and join the jejunum.

claims.text: Ileum: the longest part; it joins the cecum at the ileocecal valve.
claims.quote: The ileum is the longest part of the small intestine, measuring about 1.8 meters (6 feet) in length. It is thicker, more vascular, and has more developed mucosal folds than the jejunum. The ileum joins the cecum, the first portion of the large intestine, at the ileocecal sphincter (or valve).

claims.text: Large intestine: cecum, colon, rectum and anus.
claims.quote: The large intestine is subdivided into four main regions: the cecum, the colon, the rectum, and the anus.

claims.text: Appendix: a winding tube attached to the cecum.
claims.quote: The appendix (or vermiform appendix) is a winding tube that attaches to the cecum.

claims.text: Colon path: ascending colon on the right, hepatic (right colic) flexure under the liver, transverse colon, splenic (left colic) flexure under the spleen, descending colon on the left, then the S-shaped sigmoid colon in the pelvis.
claims.quote: Upon entering the colon, the food residue first travels up the ascending colon on the right side of the abdomen. At the inferior surface of the liver, the colon bends to form the right colic flexure (hepatic flexure) and becomes the transverse colon. The region defined as hindgut begins with the last third of the transverse colon and continues on. Food residue passing through the transverse colon travels across to the left side of the abdomen, where the colon angles sharply immediately inferior to the spleen, at the left colic flexure (splenic flexure). From there, food residue passes through the descending colon, which runs down the left side of the posterior abdominal wall. After entering the pelvis inferiorly, it becomes the s-shaped sigmoid colon, which extends medially to the midline
